title: Psalms Chapter 72 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 72 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 72 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 72.

questions.question: Who is the Psalm 72 a Psalm for?
questions.correctAnswer: Solomon
questions.explanation: The chapter begins with 'A Psalm for Solomon' (Psalms 72:1), indicating it is dedicated to him.

questions.question: According to Psalms 72, what should God give to the king’s son?
questions.correctAnswer: Judgments and righteousness
questions.explanation: Verse 1 states, 'Give the king thy judgments, O God, and thy righteousness unto the king's son.'

questions.question: What kind of judgment shall the king give to the poor?
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment with judgment
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:2 states, 'He shall judge thy people with righteousness, and thy poor with judgment.'

questions.question: What will the mountains bring to the people according to Psalms 72?
questions.correctAnswer: Peace
questions.explanation: Verse 3 says, 'The mountains shall bring peace to the people, and the little hills, by righteousness.'

questions.question: Which group will the king save as mentioned in Psalms 72?
questions.correctAnswer: The children of the needy
questions.explanation: Verse 4 states, 'he shall save the children of the needy.'

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 72, the oppressor will be broken in pieces by the king.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:4 states, 'and shall break in pieces the oppressor.'

questions.question: How long shall people fear God according to Psalms 72?
options: As long as the sun and moon endure
questions.correctAnswer: As long as the sun and moon endure
questions.explanation: Verse 5 says, 'They shall fear thee as long as the sun and moon endure, throughout all generations.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 72 states the king shall come down like fire upon the grass.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:6 states, 'He shall come down like rain upon the mown grass,' not fire.

questions.question: What will flourish in the king’s days according to Psalms 72?
questions.correctAnswer: The righteous
questions.explanation: Verse 7 says, 'In his days shall the righteous flourish.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 72 says that abundance of peace will last as long as the moon endureth.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:7 states, 'and abundance of peace so long as the moon endureth.'

questions.question: In Psalms 72, what is compared to showers that water the earth?
questions.correctAnswer: The king’s coming down
questions.explanation: Verse 6 describes, 'He shall come down like rain upon the mown grass: as showers that water the earth.'

questions.question: Which of these comes first in Psalms 72?
options: The kings of Tarshish bring presents
The mountains shall bring peace to the people
The king shall save the children of the needy
questions.correctAnswer: The mountains shall bring peace to the people
questions.explanation: Verse 3 mentions the mountains bringing peace before the other events listed in later verses.

questions.question: Who does Psalms 72 say the king shall judge with righteousness?
questions.correctAnswer: The people
questions.explanation: Verse 2 states, 'He shall judge thy people with righteousness.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 72 says the king shall judge the wealthy and mighty with favor.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The chapter emphasizes judging the poor and needy, not the wealthy and mighty (Psalms 72:2-4).

questions.question: What natural elements are used in Psalms 72 to describe the king’s rule?
questions.correctAnswer: Rain and showers
questions.explanation: Verse 6 describes the king’s coming down as 'like rain upon the mown grass: as showers that water the earth.'

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 72 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 72 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 72:8, what extent of dominion will the king have?
options: From sea to sea, and from the river unto the ends of the earth
From the mountains to the valley
Only over the land of Israel
Over the cities of the east
questions.correctAnswer: From sea to sea, and from the river unto the ends of the earth
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:8 explicitly states that the king will have dominion from sea to sea and from the river unto the ends of the earth, indicating a vast and universal reign.

questions.question: What will happen to the enemies of the king according to Psalms 72:9?
questions.correctAnswer: They shall lick the dust
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:9 says that the enemies shall lick the dust, symbolizing their defeat and submission to the king's authority.

questions.question: Who will bring presents to the king as mentioned in Psalms 72:10?
options: The kings of Tarshish and of the isles
questions.correctAnswer: The kings of Tarshish and of the isles
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:10 states that the kings of Tarshish and of the isles will bring presents, while the kings of Sheba and Seba will offer gifts, indicating honor and recognition of the king's status.

questions.question: What is the response of all kings and nations to the king described in Psalms 72:11?
options: All kings shall fall down before him and all nations shall serve him
They shall wage war against him
They shall seek to overthrow him
questions.correctAnswer: All kings shall fall down before him and all nations shall serve him
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:11 declares that all kings will fall down before him and all nations will serve him, showing universal submission and worship.

questions.question: According to Psalms 72:12, whom will the king deliver?
options: The needy when he crieth, the poor also, and him that hath no helper
questions.correctAnswer: The needy when he crieth, the poor also, and him that hath no helper
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:12 highlights the king's role as a deliverer of the needy and poor, especially those without help, emphasizing compassion and justice.

questions.question: How does Psalms 72:13 describe the king's treatment of the poor and needy?
options: He shall spare them and save their souls
questions.correctAnswer: He shall spare them and save their souls
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:13 states that the king shall spare the poor and needy and save their souls, showing mercy and salvation as key aspects of his reign.

questions.question: What does Psalms 72:14 say the king will redeem the needy from?
questions.correctAnswer: Deceit and violence
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:14 reveals that the king will redeem the needy from deceit and violence, highlighting his protective and just nature toward the vulnerable.

questions.question: What lesson about humility and submission can we learn from Psalms 72:9 and 72:11?
options: All peoples and kings will eventually bow before God's appointed king
Only specific tribes will serve the king
The king will rule with force and fear only
questions.correctAnswer: All peoples and kings will eventually bow before God's appointed king
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:9 and 72:11 together teach that all who dwell in wilderness and all kings will bow and fall down before the king, demonstrating the universal authority and reverence owed to God's anointed.

questions.question: Based on Psalms 72:12-13, how should a believer respond to those in need?
options: By delivering, sparing, and saving the needy as the king does
By ignoring their cry for help
By expecting them to help themselves
questions.correctAnswer: By delivering, sparing, and saving the needy as the king does
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:12-13 shows the king's compassionate care for the needy; believers are taught to emulate this by actively helping and protecting those in need.

questions.question: What promise does Psalms 72:8 give about the scope of the king's rule, and how might this encourage faith in God's plan?
options: The king's dominion will extend universally, encouraging trust in God's sovereign plan
The king will rule only a small territory, limiting hope
The king will share power equally with enemies
The king's rule will be temporary and weak
questions.correctAnswer: The king's dominion will extend universally, encouraging trust in God's sovereign plan
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:8 promises dominion from sea to sea, emphasizing God's control over all nations, which encourages believers to trust in His sovereign and comprehensive plan.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 72:10 teaches that kings of distant lands will acknowledge and honor the king by bringing gifts.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:10 clearly states that the kings of Tarshish and the isles, as well as kings of Sheba and Seba, will bring presents and offer gifts, showing respect and honor.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 72:14, the king considers the blood of the needy to be of little value.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:14 says that precious shall their blood be in his sight, indicating the king highly values and protects the lives of the needy.

questions.question: What does Psalms 72:9-11 combined teach about the king's relationship with his enemies and the nations?
options: Enemies will submit and all nations will serve the king
Enemies will be ignored and nations will rebel
The king will isolate from other nations
Nations will compete against the king
questions.correctAnswer: Enemies will submit and all nations will serve the king
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:9-11 teaches that those dwelling in wilderness will bow, enemies will lick the dust, and all kings and nations will serve the king, showing total submission and service.

questions.question: If a believer prays for deliverance as mentioned in Psalms 72:12, what does Psalms 72:13 assure about God's response?
options: God will spare and save the needy
questions.correctAnswer: God will spare and save the needy
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:12 promises deliverance to the needy when they cry; Psalms 72:13 assures that God will spare and save their souls, encouraging believers to trust in His help.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 72:8-14 collectively emphasize that the king's rule is marked by justice, mercy, and universal authority.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verses 8 through 14 describe dominion from sea to sea, submission of enemies, gifts from kings, care for the needy, and redemption from violence, highlighting justice, mercy, and authority.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 72 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 72.

questions.question: According to Psalms 72:15, what is given to the king alongside continual prayer and daily praise?
questions.correctAnswer: Gold of Sheba
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:15 states that gold of Sheba shall be given to him, and prayer shall be made for him continually with daily praise.

questions.question: What agricultural imagery is used in Psalms 72:16 to describe prosperity?
options: A handful of corn on the mountains
questions.correctAnswer: A handful of corn on the mountains
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:16 uses the imagery of a handful of corn on the mountains and fruit shaking like Lebanon to depict abundance and flourishing.

questions.question: Which phrase from Psalms 72:17 expresses the enduring legacy of the king?
questions.correctAnswer: His name shall endure forever
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:17 declares that his name shall endure forever and be continued as long as the sun.

questions.question: Psalms 72:18 blesses the LORD God for doing what kind of deeds?
questions.correctAnswer: Wondrous things
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:18 specifically blesses the LORD God who only does wondrous things.

questions.question: What is the final declaration in Psalms 72:19 regarding the LORD's glory?
options: The whole earth shall be filled with His glory
His glory shall be confined to Israel
His glory will fade with time
The nations will reject His glory
questions.correctAnswer: The whole earth shall be filled with His glory
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:19 declares that the whole earth shall be filled with the LORD's glory, ending with 'Amen, and Amen.'

questions.question: Who is identified as the author of the prayers in Psalms 72:20?
questions.correctAnswer: David the son of Jesse
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:20 clearly states that these are the prayers of David the son of Jesse.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage shares the theme of the king's righteous reign and universal dominion as seen in Psalms 72:8?
questions.correctAnswer: Daniel 7:13-14
questions.explanation: Daniel 7:13-14 also speaks of a dominion from sea to sea given to the 'Son of man,' echoing the theme of universal reign in Psalms 72:8.

questions.question: The phrase 'prayer also shall be made for him continually' in Psalms 72:15 foreshadows which New Testament practice?
options: Intercessory prayer for Jesus as King
questions.correctAnswer: Intercessory prayer for Jesus as King
questions.explanation: The continual prayer for the king in Psalms 72:15 foreshadows the New Testament practice of intercessory prayer for Jesus as the eternal King.

questions.question: In Psalms 72:16, what does the shaking of the fruit 'like Lebanon' symbolize in the ancient Near Eastern context?
questions.correctAnswer: Great abundance and fertility
questions.explanation: Lebanon was renowned for its fertile cedars and abundant fruit; thus, the shaking fruit symbolizes plentiful harvest and prosperity (Psalms 72:16).

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Psalms 72:15-19 to emphasize the king's blessedness and God's glory?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: These verses employ parallelism by repeating similar blessings and praises to emphasize the king’s blessedness and the LORD’s glory (Psalms 72:15-19).

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word translated as 'redeem' in Psalms 72:14, and how does it deepen understanding of the king's role?
options: To ransom or rescue from bondage
questions.correctAnswer: To ransom or rescue from bondage
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'redeem' in Psalms 72:14 means to ransom or rescue, highlighting the king’s role as a deliverer from deceit and violence.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 72:17 states that all nations will call the king blessed and that men shall be blessed in him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:17 explicitly says all nations shall call him blessed and men shall be blessed in him.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 72:18, the God of Israel is praised for His mighty wars and conquests.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:18 praises the LORD God for doing only wondrous things, not specifically mighty wars or conquests.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of an eternal kingdom and blessedness of the King as found in Psalms 72:17?
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation 22:5
questions.explanation: Revelation 22:5 speaks of the saints reigning forever with the Lord, echoing the eternal kingdom and blessing theme of Psalms 72:17.

questions.question: How does Psalms 72:19 serve as a concluding doxology, and what is its significance in the structure of the psalm?
options: It praises God's glorious name forever, forming a liturgical ending
It introduces a new theme of judgment
It recounts the king’s military victories
questions.correctAnswer: It praises God's glorious name forever, forming a liturgical ending
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:19 closes with a doxology praising God's glorious name forever, marking a liturgical conclusion to the psalm.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 72 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 72 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What specific divine attribute is highlighted by the prayer for the king to judge with righteousness and justice?
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice and righteousness
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:1-2 emphasizes the king receiving God's judgments and righteousness, highlighting God's attribute of justice and righteousness as foundational for righteous governance.

questions.question: According to Psalms 72:4, what role does the king have in relation to the oppressed and needy?
options: To break in pieces the oppressor and save the needy
questions.correctAnswer: To break in pieces the oppressor and save the needy
questions.explanation: Verse 4 clearly states that the king shall save the children of the needy and break the oppressor, emphasizing a role of deliverance and protection.

questions.question: What metaphor is used in Psalms 72:6 to describe the king's coming and its effect on the earth?
options: Rain upon mown grass and showers that water the earth
questions.correctAnswer: Rain upon mown grass and showers that water the earth
questions.explanation: Verse 6 uses the metaphor of rain and showers to depict the king's coming as life-giving and refreshing, symbolizing blessing and restoration.

questions.question: Which doctrine is primarily taught by the promise that 'the righteous shall flourish' and 'abundance of peace' during the king's days?
options: The doctrine of the Messianic Kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of the Messianic Kingdom
questions.explanation: Psalms 72:7 anticipates a reign marked by righteousness and peace, reflecting the Messianic Kingdom where God's rule brings flourishing and shalom.

questions.question: What does the king's dominion 'from sea to sea, and from the river unto the ends of the earth' signify theologically?
options: Universal sovereignty of the messianic king
questions.correctAnswer: Universal sovereignty of the messianic king
questions.explanation: Verse 8 describes dominion spanning all lands, symbolizing God's universal rule manifested through the king, a key aspect of biblical kingship and Messiah's reign.

questions.question: How does Psalms 72:10-11 portray the response of the nations to the king?
options: They bring gifts and fall down before him
questions.correctAnswer: They bring gifts and fall down before him
questions.explanation: Verses 10-11 depict foreign kings bringing presents and all nations serving the king, indicating recognition and submission to his authority.

questions.question: What theological truth is expressed in Psalms 72:12-13 regarding God's care for the vulnerable?
options: God delivers and spares the needy and helpless
God is indifferent to human suffering
questions.correctAnswer: God delivers and spares the needy and helpless
questions.explanation: These verses affirm God's compassion and deliverance of the needy and helpless, emphasizing His covenantal care and justice.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight emerges from Psalms 72:14 and 72:15 about the king's attitude towards justice and honor?
options: The king values the lives of the oppressed and is continually honored
The king ignores justice but receives gifts
The king rules harshly over enemies
The king is weak and unpraised
questions.correctAnswer: The king values the lives of the oppressed and is continually honored
questions.explanation: Verse 14 shows the king redeems souls from violence and values their blood; verse 15 speaks of continual prayer and praise for him, linking justice and honor.

questions.question: How does Psalms 72:16 illustrate the blessing of agricultural abundance and urban prosperity under the king's reign?
options: A handful of corn on mountains and flourishing cities
questions.correctAnswer: A handful of corn on mountains and flourishing cities
questions.explanation: Verse 16 metaphorically describes abundant crops and thriving cities, symbolizing divine blessing and peace in both rural and urban settings.

questions.question: What does Psalms 72:17 teach about the enduring nature of the king’s name and its blessing to all nations?
options: His name endures forever and all nations call him blessed
His name is only known locally
His name causes fear but no blessing
questions.correctAnswer: His name endures forever and all nations call him blessed
questions.explanation: Verse 17 promises an everlasting name and universal blessing, reflecting eternal kingship and the blessing of the nations through him.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is praised in Psalms 72:18, highlighting His unique capability?
options: God is the only one who does wondrous things
questions.correctAnswer: God is the only one who does wondrous things
questions.explanation: Verse 18 blesses the LORD as the God of Israel who alone performs wondrous deeds, emphasizing His uniqueness and power.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Psalms 72 merely praises a human king with no divine significance. What does Psalms 72:5-6 and 72:11 actually teach about the nature of this king’s reign?
options: The king's reign is divinely ordained, eternal, and universally acknowledged
The king is a mere earthly ruler with limited power
The king relies solely on military might
The king is unknown and unrecognized
questions.correctAnswer: The king's reign is divinely ordained, eternal, and universally acknowledged
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 describe enduring fear of God and life-giving blessings, while verse 11 shows all nations serving him, indicating divine authority and universal recognition, not just human kingship.

questions.question: What combined theological theme arises from Psalms 72:3 and 72:7 regarding the effects of righteousness in the king’s reign?
options: Righteousness brings peace and flourishing to the land and people
questions.correctAnswer: Righteousness brings peace and flourishing to the land and people
questions.explanation: Verse 3 connects righteousness with peace from the mountains and hills, and verse 7 speaks of righteous flourishing and abundant peace, showing righteousness' restorative effect.

questions.question: How does Psalms 72:9 contribute to the overall redemptive narrative concerning the king’s victory over opposition?
options: Enemies are humbled, bowing and licking the dust, signifying complete defeat
Enemies form alliances with the king
questions.correctAnswer: Enemies are humbled, bowing and licking the dust, signifying complete defeat
questions.explanation: Verse 9 depicts the wilderness dwellers bowing and the enemies licking dust, symbolizing total victory and submission, a key element in God's redemptive triumph over evil.

questions.question: What doctrine is illustrated by the king’s role in redeeming souls from deceit and violence as stated in Psalms 72:14?
options: The doctrine of salvation and redemption
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of salvation and redemption
questions.explanation: Verse 14 shows the king redeeming souls from deceit and violence, highlighting the salvific role of the king as redeemer.
